findings.title: Failed USE now drops connection and marks node broken instead of keeping it
findings.claim: The new Err(ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace) branch sets had_error_since_last_refill and, when the pool empties, calls update_shared_conns publishing the pool as Broken(ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError), so a keyspace-level failure can fail every query to that node and potentially take down the whole session; previously the connection was still added to the pool.

findings.title: USE-failure branch skips immediate non-shard-aware retry done by the Connection branch
findings.claim: The branch skips the immediate non-shard-aware retry that the Connection branch does for requested_shard.is_some(), so a failed shard-aware connection waits for the backed-off refill instead of retrying immediately, causing churn and metric noise on persistent failure.

findings.title: USE failure log level dropped from warn! to debug!, making failures invisible at default…
findings.claim: The old code logged warn! in start_setting_keyspace_for_connection, but the new debug! in handle_ready_connection is invisible at default log levels; a partial failure (some connections dropped, others fine) is now silent.

findings.title: Unrelated metric fixes bundled into PR beyond the stated keyspace fix scope
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections calls on clearing excess connections and on resharding (plus three tests) are not mentioned in the PR title or description, widening review and revert scope beyond the Fixes: #1682 keyspace fix; the description should mention them or they should go in a separate PR.
